title: Front brake pads and rotors
setting: Small independent shop, customer's sedan on the floor, and the only lift is taken.

steps.line: Car's on the ground, cracking the lug nuts loose on both front wheels before I lift it.
Rear wheels are chocked. Floor jack under the front center jacking point, lifting till both front tires are off the ground.
Lift's taken, so I'll just leave it sitting up on the floor jack. I'm only gonna be in the wheel wells for a few minutes.

error.summary: Left the car sitting on just the floor jack
error.why: A jack is for lifting, not holding. A hydraulic jack can bleed down or roll, and Jess's hands and arms are in the wheel well the whole job.
error.correctAction: Set jack stands under the factory support points, lower the car onto them, and leave the jack snugged up underneath as a backup.
error.consequence: The jack bled down while Jess was reaching behind the rotor, and the car came down on Jess's arm. Broken arm and a trip to the emergency room.

steps.line: Wheels off. Pulling the caliper bolts and the bracket bolts on the driver side.
Letting the caliper hang off the brake hose while I swap the rotor.

error.summary: Let the caliper hang by its brake hose
error.why: The weight of the caliper can tear the rubber hose on the inside, even when it looks fine from the outside. That can cause a soft pedal or a brake that drags.
error.correctAction: Hang the caliper from the spring or strut with a hook, a bungee, or a piece of wire so there's no strain on the hose.
error.consequence: The hose tore on the inside and started trapping pressure. The customer came back a month later with that brake dragging and the car pulling to one side.

steps.line: Wire brushed the rust off the hub, new rotor's on and wiped down with brake cleaner. Fluid level's checked, now pushing the piston back with the old pad and a C clamp.
Pads in with new clips, slide pins greased, caliper's back on. Running the bracket bolts in with the impact, a couple good hits and they're tight.

error.summary: Ran the bracket bolts in with an impact, no torque
error.why: Caliper bracket bolts hold the whole brake to the knuckle and have a torque spec. An impact gun can strip the threads in the knuckle or leave the bolts loose, and there's no way to know which.
error.correctAction: Start the bolts by hand, then tighten them with a torque wrench to the factory spec, with thread locker if the manual calls for it.
error.consequence: One bracket bolt backed out over the next few weeks. The customer came back with a grinding clunk when braking, and the shop paid for a new rotor, a bracket, and a chewed up wheel.

steps.line: Same on the other side. Wheels on, lugs run down snug, car's back on the ground, then torquing the lugs in a star pattern.
Pumping the pedal till it's firm, checking the fluid level again, and taking it around the block to bed in the pads before I hand the keys back.
